back: Finding a position from its distances (ranges) to several known points; GPS uses satellite ranges.
Range = speed of light × signal travel time (c ≈ 300 000 km/s).

front: How many satellites for a 3D fix, and why?
back: Four: x, y, z and the receiver clock error are four unknowns.
Atmospheric delay, multipath, poor satellite geometry (DOP), canopy and buildings, clock and orbit errors.
A base station at a known position computes signal errors and sends corrections to nearby receivers.
Waypoint: a single recorded position. Track: positions recorded automatically as the receiver moves.
Dilution of precision: poor accuracy when satellites are bunched in the sky.
A few metres for a handheld receiver; sub-metre with differential GPS; centimetres with RTK survey methods.
Download waypoints and tracks (e.g. GPX), load as point, line or polygon layers, check datum and reproject if necessary.
